page_hint: Section 5, Common Mistakes, fifth bullet (protocol overhead)
quoted_clause: 200/400GbE transcodes 64b/66b to 256b/257b before FEC
observed: The claim that 200/400GbE 'transcodes 64b/66b to 256b/257b before FEC' needs verification against IEEE 802.3. The PCS layer for 200GBASE-R/400GBASE-R uses 64b/66b encoding; the subsequent FEC (typically RS(544,514) / KP4) operates on different block structures. The phrase 'transcodes to 256b/257b' implies a direct encoding conversion that may not accurately describe the standard's layering. Additionally, 200GbE and 400GbE may use different lane counts and FEC configurations, making the lumped '200/400GbE' claim potentially imprecise.
correction: Verify against IEEE 802.3 clauses for 200GBASE-R/400GBASE-R. If the 256b/257b reference is to a specific gearbox or FEC block size, rephrase to name the correct layer (e.g., 'the PCS uses 64b/66b; the KP4 FEC operates on 256-bit blocks'). If uncertain, simplify to: 'use the specific standard's payload-efficiency figure' without the specific encoding claim.
acceptance_test: The encoding claim should be verifiable against a specific IEEE 802.3 clause, or be removed/simplified.
verdict_evidence: chapter-09.md:144 quote ✓ and tag ✓, but the mechanism is real: an IEEE 802.3bs contribution analyzes '64/66B-256/257B transcoding' in 400GbE before FEC (ieee802.org/3/bs).
verdict_fix: No change needed; optionally cite the IEEE 802.3bs transcoding contribution to make the claim verifiable.

quoted_clause: the meaningful per-step data movement is a TP all-reduce of the per-layer activations (tens of MBs, not GBs, at the canonical batch and hidden size — it scales with batch × hidden width per layer)
observed: The parenthetical '(tens of MBs...)' is ambiguous: it could refer to each per-layer all-reduce or to the per-step total across all layers. For a 70B model with hidden_size ≈ 8192, batch 32, FP16, each per-layer activation all-reduce is ~512 KB (sub-MB), while the per-step total across ~80 layers is ~40 MB (tens of MBs). The phrase 'it scales with batch × hidden width per layer' suggests the per-step total, but the proximity to 'per-layer activations' invites the per-layer reading.
correction: Rephrase to: 'the per-step total across all layers is tens of MBs (each individual per-layer all-reduce is sub-MB at the canonical batch and hidden size).'
acceptance_test: A reader should be able to determine from the sentence alone whether 'tens of MBs' refers to per-layer or per-step total.

quoted_clause: samples 1,000 retrievals per cycle (n ≈ 1,000 sized for the <0.3% target at 95% confidence; 0.001 resolution)
observed: With n=1,000 and a true rate near 0.3%, the expected event count is 3. The 95% binomial CI for 3/1,000 is roughly [0.06%, 0.88%], which is far wider than the 0.3% target. n=1,000 gives a 95% upper bound of 0.3% only in the zero-event case (rule of three: 3/1,000 = 0.003). The claim 'sized for the <0.3% target at 95% confidence' is therefore only true under a zero-failure observation, not in general.
correction: Rephrase: 'n ≈ 1,000 gives 0.001 measurement granularity and a 95% zero-event upper bound of 0.3%; detecting a true rate near 0.3% with a tight CI requires a larger n (e.g., ~3,000–4,000 for a ±0.1% half-width at p≈0.003).'
acceptance_test: The text distinguishes granularity from CI width and does not claim n=1,000 is sufficient to estimate a 0.3% rate with a tight 95% CI.

page_hint: Ch 17 §4, bullet 'The 25 ms/token in W is the TPOT budget, not a measured per-step time'; also Ch 15 §3 'Compute demand versus peak' and Ch 17 §4 'Simultaneous feasibility check'

The inference 'a well-tuned decode can run well under the 25 ms SLO' therefore does not follow at the canonical context length and concurrency. The same omission makes the decode leg's feasibility at the canonical peak invisible: 12,000 output tok/s x (140/B + 24.1) GB/token ≈ 388 TB/s at B = 17, roughly 14x the host's HBM bandwidth.
correction: Add the KV term: bytes/step = 140 GB + B x 24.9 GB; step time = that / 26.8 TB/s; at B = 17 -> ~21 ms/step. Re-anchor the Ch 17 sensitivity band (currently 5.2/10/25 ms) to the true floor, and add the decode-leg HBM feasibility check at the canonical peak so the reader sees decode, like prefill, is a fleet-level constraint at 40 rps. Also revisit the FLOP-based '~21 %' decode ratio in Ch 15 §3, which is not the informative measure for a bandwidth-bound phase.

verdict_evidence: ch17:124 floor 140÷(8×3.35)=5.2ms omits KV; 140+17×24.9037=563.4GB ÷26.8TB/s=21.0ms; ch15:9 names KV-read traffic but never quantifies it.
